hook: A gentle, melancholy anomaly: a man whose surroundings rearrange themselves to keep his ordinary life exactly as it was. There is no monster here, only an office worker and a routine he cannot step out of. The file is short, and the closing interview is the part that tends to stay with you.
whyItMatters: It is a quieter take on reality-bending, where the power serves no ambition and simply protects an unchanging status quo. The incident reports read almost like comedy, turning an armoured vehicle and a maintenance closet into pieces of his commute and his cubicle. The format is used to say something about loneliness and stalled lives rather than about danger.
thingsToNotice: The procedures are mostly about accommodating him, which tells you how harmless and how fixed he is before the description does. Each incident repeats the same pattern of Foundation space turning back into his old world, and the repetition becomes the point. In the interview, watch the researcher stop correcting him and start playing along; the humour and the sadness share the same lines.
